Thanks,

Hi Sara, Markus —

Following our quick sync this morning, I've sketched a practical set of options and the associated risk register. See summary below; full MAP v2 attached (stub).

Summary of options (pros / cons):
1) Procurement Exception (short-term)
   - Pro: preserves acceptance window; low engineering effort
   - Con: procurement/legal must accept compensating controls; temporary exposure window
2) Parallelized Eval (limited dataset)
   - Pro: keeps go/no-go cadence intact; reduces sensitive data exposure
   - Con: additional ops runbook and test harness required; more work for Helix team
3) Rebaseline Acceptance by 10 business days
   - Pro: buys runway for security review; reduces operational overhead
   - Con: executive / financial timeline impact; requires formal change request in MAP

Recommended: start with Option 1 while we run Option 2 in parallel. If procurement declines, we fall back to Option 3 and trigger the escalation play we've documented.

Action items:
- Markus: confirm procurement language / PO requirement (today)
- Sara: please share procurement contact and any written exception template
- Karthik: provide ETA for the limited-dataset eval harness + estimated engineer-hours (EOD 1/16)

Attached: MAP-v2.xlsx (outline, milestones, proposed new acceptance date), risk_log_snippet.csv

Laura Bennett
